scenes.heading: Rates of reaction
scenes.sub: Why are fireworks fast but rust so slow?
scenes.say: Fireworks explode in a flash, but an iron gate takes years to rust. Why do some reactions go so much faster than others?

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A high five needs meeting, force and lining up
scenes.science: Particles must collide, with enough energy, the right way
scenes.breaks: People choose to high five; particles move randomly and have no choice in how they collide.
scenes.say: Collision theory is like a high five at a party. You have to meet, swing hard enough, and line your hands up. Particles must collide, with at least the activation energy, and with the right orientation. Hit, hard enough, right way round. Only then is it a successful collision.

scenes.heading: Try Catching Some Cats
scenes.say: There are four ways to speed up a reaction. Remember: Try Catching Some Cats. Temperature, concentration or pressure, surface area, and catalyst.

scenes.heading: How they work
scenes.say: Concentration, pressure and surface area all make collisions more frequent. Temperature mainly works differently: a bigger fraction of collisions have enough energy. Always say per second, because rate is about time.
scenes.caption: Concentration, pressure and surface area all make collisions more frequent. Temperature mainly works differently: a bigger fraction of collisions have enough energy. Always say 'per second', because rate is about time.

scenes.heading: Catalysts
scenes.everyday: A tunnel through the hill you'd otherwise ride over
scenes.science: A catalyst gives a path with lower activation energy
scenes.breaks: A tunnel just sits there; a catalyst takes part briefly, then is released unchanged.
scenes.say: Activation energy is like a hill you must ride over. A catalyst is a tunnel through the hill: a different path with a lower barrier. It doesn't give particles more energy, and it isn't used up. Enzymes, like amylase in your saliva, are biological catalysts.

scenes.heading: Average rate
scenes.question: Marble chips react with acid. 36 mL of CO₂ is made in 30 s, and 60 mL by 60 s. Find the rate between 30 s and 60 s.
scenes.say: Average rate is the change in product divided by the time taken. Between thirty and sixty seconds, the gas went from thirty-six to sixty millilitres. That's twenty-four millilitres in thirty seconds, or zero point eight zero millilitres per second.
scenes.caption: Average rate is the change in product divided by the time taken. Between 30 and 60 seconds, the gas went from 36 to 60 mL. That's 24 mL in 30 s, or 0.80 mL s⁻¹.

scenes.heading: Reading rate graphs
points: Faster run: steeper, levels off sooner
scenes.say: On a graph of gas against time, steep means fast and flat means finished. If you use powder instead of chips, the curve is steeper and levels off sooner. But with the same amounts of reactants, it ends at the same height. A faster reaction doesn't make more product.

points: Hit, hard enough, right way round
Catalysts lower Eₐ, not used up
scenes.say: Quick recap. Particles must hit, hard enough, the right way round. Temperature, concentration, surface area and catalysts speed things up. Catalysts lower the activation energy. Steep is fast, flat is finished. Now try the practice questions!
